reading.body:
Three major open-source frameworks for voice and service agents have accumulated over 40,000 GitHub stars combined, with the largest reaching 15,000 stars, indicating significant developer adoption in this category.

Voice agent frameworks are standardizing around Python and real-time communication primitives. Each framework handles the latency-sensitive pipeline from audio input through inference to synthesis and output, which means they are built for compute efficiency rather than batch processing. This reflects a shift from the server-side constraint model: voice agents must run continuously and responsively, turning each interaction into a live compute demand on infrastructure.

The frameworks are maintained by infrastructure companies, Daily and LiveKit, rather than traditional software vendors. This matters because voice agents require reliable networking and low-latency pipelines as much as they require model capability. A voice agent's usefulness depends on end-to-end latency, which ties computational demands directly to network and power infrastructure rather than raw model size.

The data covers only three projects and does not indicate adoption by end-users, production deployment scale, or the power consumption of running these agents at volume. It shows developer interest in the tooling, not the underlying infrastructure load these tools create.
